Start with free tools: Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools for indexing and search data, Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema.org validator for structured data, and a site audit tool for technical issues. Add Semrush or Ahrefs for research, plus an AI visibility tracker for citations.
- [How much does SEO cost?](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/seo-cost): Most US businesses pay for SEO as a monthly retainer. Local, single-location work often starts around $1,000 to $2,000 a month, while competitive or multi-location programs commonly run several thousand dollars or more. Price depends on competition, site size, content volume and link building. Our own plans start at $1,500 a month.
- [What is the best strategy for SEO?](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/best-seo-strategy): The best SEO strategy is the one that fits your business, competition and starting point. For most sites that means fixing technical problems first, mapping keywords to search intent, publishing content that shows real experience, linking pages internally, earning authority, strengthening local signals where relevant, and making content easy for AI answers to cite.
- [What is the best SEO tool?](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/best-seo-tools): There is no single best SEO tool. Google Search Console is the most important free tool because it shows how Google sees your site. Pair it with Google Analytics 4 for conversions, a crawler like Screaming Frog for technical audits, and a paid suite such as Semrush, Ahrefs or Moz for keyword and backlink research.
- [How can SEO be improved?](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/how-to-improve-seo): To improve SEO, fix technical issues that block crawling and indexing, match each page to one search intent, refresh content that is outdated, add internal links between related pages, show real expertise and trust, earn relevant links, strengthen local signals, and measure results in Search Console and Analytics so you can repeat what works.
- [How to track SEO rankings](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/track-seo-rankings): Track SEO rankings by combining Google Search Console's Performance report, which shows average position from real impressions, with a rank tracker that checks fixed keywords by device and location. Add map-pack grid tracking for local businesses and manual or tool-based checks of AI answers. Report trends monthly, tied to clicks and leads.
- [How to do SEO keyword research](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/seo-keyword-research): To do SEO keyword research, start with the words customers use, expand them with keyword tools, and check search intent by studying the results page. Weigh difficulty against business value, group related terms into clusters, and assign each cluster to one page. Add local modifiers and question keywords so pages can answer searches and AI prompts directly.
- [What is SEO link building?](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/what-is-link-building): SEO link building is the work of earning links from other websites to yours. Search engines treat relevant links from trusted sites as a signal that your pages are credible and worth ranking. Good link building uses digital PR, useful content, partnerships and local relationships, and avoids paid or manipulative links that break Google's spam policies.
- [What is SEO schema for real estate?](https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/real-estate-schema): Real estate schema is structured data, usually in JSON-LD, that describes agents, brokerages, listings and events using schema.org types such as RealEstateAgent, Person, SingleFamilyResidence, Offer and Event. Google has no dedicated US listing rich result, so the value lies in clearer entity signals, eligibility for general features like breadcrumbs, and better understanding by AI systems.

## What is SEO?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/what-is-seo

**Short answer:** SEO (search engine optimization) is the work of making a website easier for search engines to crawl, understand and trust, so its pages show up for the searches your customers make. It covers technical health, useful content, on-page signals, links and reviews from other sites, and local listings. Results usually build over several months.

- SEO helps the right pages show up when people search for what you sell.
- Search engines crawl, index and then rank pages based on relevance and quality.
- Technical, on-page, off-page and local SEO each solve a different problem.
- AI search tools draw on the same foundations, so solid SEO still matters.

### SEO in one paragraph

Search engine optimization is the practice of improving a website so it earns more visits from unpaid search results. When someone types or speaks a question into Google, Bing or an AI assistant, the engine picks the pages it believes answer that question best. SEO is the work of making your pages the ones it picks. That work spans your site's code, your content, your reputation across the web and your business listings.

SEO differs from paid search. With ads, you pay for each click and the traffic stops when the budget stops. With SEO, you invest in pages and signals that keep earning visits over time. Most US businesses that rely on search use both, with SEO doing the steady, compounding work underneath.

Good SEO is also good for people. Fast pages, clear answers, honest information and easy navigation help visitors and search engines in the same way. Google's public guidance says it aims to reward helpful, reliable content made for people, and that is a sound target for any site.
### How search engines crawl, index and rank pages

Search engines work in three broad stages. First they crawl, which means automated programs follow links and sitemaps to discover pages. Then they index, which means they process each page, work out what it is about and store it in a huge database. Finally they rank, which means they sort indexed pages for each search and decide the order of results.

Problems at any stage stop a page from performing. A page that can't be crawled won't be found. A page that is found but blocked, duplicated or thin may never be indexed. A page that is indexed but weak on relevance or trust will sit too low for anyone to see it.

Ranking systems weigh many signals. Google describes the broad factors in its public documentation: the meaning of the query, the relevance of the content, its quality, the usability of the page and the context of the searcher, such as location. No one outside Google knows the exact weighting, so be wary of anyone who claims to.

- Crawl: bots discover URLs through links, sitemaps and submissions.

- Index: the engine reads, renders and stores the page if it qualifies.

- Rank: indexed pages are ordered for each query by relevance and quality.

- Serve: results appear as blue links, map listings, rich results or AI summaries.
### On-page, off-page and technical SEO

SEO work is usually grouped into three areas. Each one answers a different question a search engine asks about your site. You need all three working together, because a strong page on a broken site, or a fast site with nothing worth reading, will struggle.

On-page SEO is about the content and signals on each page. That includes the topic you target, how well you answer the searcher's question, titles, headings, internal links, images and structured data. Off-page SEO is about your reputation elsewhere, mainly links from other sites, brand mentions and reviews. Technical SEO is about the plumbing: crawlability, indexing rules, site speed, mobile usability, security and clean site architecture.

| Area | Question it answers | Typical work |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Technical SEO | Can search engines access and process the site? | Crawl and index fixes, site speed, mobile usability, redirects, sitemaps, structured data |

| On-page SEO | Does this page answer the search well? | Keyword and intent research, content, titles, headings, internal links, media |

| Off-page SEO | Do other people vouch for this site? | Earned links, digital PR, brand mentions, reviews, citations |

| Local SEO | Is this business relevant and trusted nearby? | Google Business Profile, local pages, NAP consistency, reviews |
### Local SEO for businesses that serve an area

If you serve customers in a city or region, local SEO is often where the fastest wins are. Searches like "plumber near me" or "dentist in Austin" show a map pack of nearby businesses before the regular results. Getting into that pack depends heavily on your Google Business Profile, your reviews and how close you are to the searcher.

The basics are simple to list and take discipline to maintain. Fill out your Google Business Profile completely and choose accurate categories. Keep your business name, address and phone number consistent across your site and the major directories. Ask happy customers for reviews and reply to them. Build a clear page for each core service and each area you genuinely serve.

Local SEO also connects to the rest of your site. Strong service pages, good technical health and links from local organizations all help your map listing as well as your organic rankings. Treat it as one program rather than a separate project.
### How AI search changes SEO

AI answers now appear in many places, including Google's AI Overviews, Bing's Copilot, ChatGPT and Perplexity. These tools often summarize an answer and cite a few sources instead of showing ten links. That changes how people click, and it raises the value of being one of the sources the answer is built from.

The good news is that the foundations are the same. AI search systems still need to find, read and trust your content. Pages that are crawlable, clearly structured, factually accurate and backed by real expertise are the ones most likely to be used. Work focused on this is often called answer engine optimization (AEO) or generative engine optimization (GEO).

In practice, that means writing direct answers near the top of a page, using clear headings that match real questions, adding accurate structured data and keeping facts about your business consistent across the web. It also means measuring visibility in AI answers alongside classic rankings, since a page can be cited without ranking first.
### How long SEO takes to work

SEO is a medium-term investment. Technical fixes can show effects within weeks once pages are recrawled. New content and authority-building usually take several months to gain traction, and competitive national terms can take longer. Your timeline depends on your site's starting point, your competition and how consistently the work gets done.

A sensible way to judge progress is to watch leading signals first. Look for more pages indexed, more impressions in Google Search Console, better positions for long-tail terms and more map views. Clicks, calls, form fills and revenue follow those signals. Anyone who promises a specific ranking by a specific date is guessing, because no agency controls Google's results.

- First weeks: audit, fix crawl and index issues, set up tracking.

- Months 1 to 3: improve key pages, publish priority content, clean up local listings.

- Months 3 to 6: build authority, expand content, refine based on data.

- Beyond 6 months: compound gains and defend positions as competitors respond.
### Where to start with your own site

Start by finding out what is holding your site back. Connect Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools, then run a crawl to surface broken pages, missing titles and indexing problems. Our free SEO audit tool checks a page live, and our free 40-point audit gives you a fuller picture with a human review.

Next, list the searches your best customers make and match each one to a page. Improve the pages that already get impressions before writing new ones. Fix your Google Business Profile if you serve a local area. Then build a steady rhythm of useful content and genuine outreach.

If you'd rather have help, Best SEO Company runs technical, content, local, link building and AI visibility work for US businesses. Plans start at $1,500 per month, move to month-to-month after a 90-day start term and come with plain reporting on what was done and what changed.

**Is SEO still worth it with AI search?** Yes. AI search tools still rely on pages they can crawl, understand and trust, which is what SEO builds. The way you measure success broadens to include citations in AI answers, but the core work stays the same.
**Can I do SEO myself?** Many small businesses handle the basics themselves, such as their Google Business Profile, page titles and simple content updates. Technical problems, competitive keywords and link building usually take more time and specialist skill. A free audit is a good way to see which category your site falls into.
**What is the difference between SEO and SEM?** SEO focuses on earning unpaid search results. SEM usually refers to paid search ads, though some people use it to mean both. Paid ads stop when spending stops, while SEO gains tend to build over time.
**Does SEO guarantee first-page rankings?** No. Search engines control their own results, and no honest agency can guarantee a position. What good SEO can do is remove barriers, improve relevance and quality, and raise your odds of ranking for searches that matter.

## What is the best SEO agency for the U.S. market?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/best-seo-agency-usa

**Short answer:** There is no single best SEO agency for every U.S. business. The best agency for you has proven experience in your market, uses white-hat methods, reports transparently, offers fair contract terms and can show verifiable results. Match the agency type, whether freelancer, boutique, full-service or enterprise, to your size, goals and budget.

- The right agency depends on your size, market, goals and budget.
- Judge agencies on verifiable work, clear reporting and who does the work.
- Walk away from guarantees, secret methods and long lock-in contracts.
- Compare freelancers, boutiques, full-service and enterprise firms on fit.

### Why there is no single best SEO agency

Search for "best SEO agency" and you will find many lists, and most of them are paid placements or self-promotion. The honest answer is that the best agency depends on who you are. A two-location dental practice, a national ecommerce brand and a B2B software company need different skills, team sizes and budgets.

An agency that excels at local map rankings for home service businesses may have little experience with large ecommerce catalogs. An enterprise firm built for global brands may be too slow and too expensive for a regional company. Fit matters more than reputation in the abstract.

So instead of hunting for a winner, define what you need. Write down your goals, your markets, your internal resources and your budget. Then use the criteria below to find agencies that match, and test their claims before you sign.
### What to look for in a US SEO agency

The US market has its own search behavior, competition levels and local nuances. An agency that works mostly with US businesses will understand state-by-state local search, American spelling and phrasing, US review platforms and the competitive intensity of major metro areas. That experience shortens the learning curve.

Beyond market knowledge, look for evidence of how the agency works. You want clear strategy tied to business outcomes, methods that follow Google's spam policies and reporting you can understand without a translator. You also want to know exactly who will touch your account.

- US market experience: work with businesses like yours, in markets like yours.

- Local vs national fit: map-pack and Google Business Profile skill for local firms, content and authority scale for national ones.

- Transparent reporting: rankings, traffic, leads and the work completed each month, with access to your own data.

- White-hat methods: no paid link schemes, private blog networks or spun content.

- Fair contracts: clear scope, reasonable minimum terms and a simple exit.

- Verifiable case studies: results you can check, with permission to contact the client.

- Who does the work: in-house staff or named specialists, not an anonymous outsourcing chain.
### Comparing agency types

Most SEO providers fall into one of four types. Each has real strengths, and each suits a different kind of business. Use the table to narrow your shortlist before you start calls.

Price ranges vary widely by region and scope, so ask each provider for a written proposal. Compare what is included, how much senior time you get and what you own at the end, rather than comparing headline monthly fees alone.

| Agency type | Best for | Pros | Cons |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Freelancer | Small sites, tight budgets, one-off projects | Lower cost, direct contact with the expert, flexible | Limited capacity, single point of failure, narrower skill set |

| Boutique agency | Small and mid-sized businesses, focused niches | Specialist depth, senior attention, faster decisions | Smaller team, may not cover paid media or development |

| Full-service agency | Businesses wanting SEO plus ads, web and social | One partner for many channels, coordinated strategy | SEO may be one service among many, risk of junior staffing |

| Enterprise agency | Large brands, big sites, multiple markets | Scale, process, broad specialist bench | Higher fees, slower pace, long contracts, less senior time for smaller accounts |
### Questions to ask before you hire

A short list of direct questions will reveal more than any sales deck. Ask the same questions of every agency on your shortlist so you can compare answers side by side. Good agencies welcome these questions and answer them plainly.

Pay attention to how specific the answers are. An agency that has done the work will talk about real problems, real fixes and how they measured the outcome. Vague answers about "proprietary methods" or "secret sauce" are a warning sign.

- What would you do in the first 90 days for a business like mine?

- Who will work on my account, and what is their experience?

- How do you build links, and can I see examples?

- What will I see in a monthly report, and do I keep access to my data?

- What are the contract terms, and how do I cancel?

- Can I speak with a current client in a similar market?

- How do you handle AI search visibility alongside traditional rankings?
### Red flags to watch for

Some warning signs show up early. Guaranteed rankings are the clearest one, because no agency controls Google's results. Google's own guidance on hiring an SEO warns against providers who make that kind of promise.

Other red flags are about control and transparency. If an agency wants to own your Google Business Profile, your analytics or your domain, you lose leverage. If they won't explain how they get links, assume the method would not survive a close look. Cheap packages promising hundreds of links a month usually mean low-quality or manipulative links that can hurt you.

Finally, watch the contract. Long lock-ins with heavy penalties, vague deliverables and reports that show only vanity metrics all make it hard to judge whether the work is paying off.

- Guaranteed #1 rankings or guaranteed traffic numbers.

- Secret or proprietary link methods they won't explain.

- The agency owns your accounts, listings or content.

- Year-long contracts with no exit and unclear deliverables.

- Case studies with no names, no dates and no way to verify.

We cover technical SEO, content, local SEO and Google Business Profile, link building and digital PR, and AI search visibility work (AEO and GEO). That makes us closest to a boutique in how we staff accounts, with broader SEO coverage than most boutiques.

You keep ownership of your accounts, content and data.

We may not be the right fit if you need a single agency for paid social, TV and SEO together, or if you need a global multi-language program. In those cases a full-service or enterprise firm may suit you better, and we will tell you so.
### How to make the final decision

Once you have two or three finalists, ask each one for a short written plan based on your actual site. A free audit is a fair way to see how an agency thinks before you pay anything. Compare the depth of their findings and whether their priorities match your business goals.

Check references, read the contract carefully and confirm who your day-to-day contact will be. Then choose the agency whose plan, people and terms you trust most. The best agency for you is the one that does good work on your site, explains it clearly and keeps earning your business every month.

You can start with our free 40-point audit or run our free live SEO audit tool to see where your site stands today.

**How much does an SEO agency cost in the US?** Costs vary widely by scope, competition and agency type. Freelancers often charge less than agencies, and enterprise firms charge the most. Compare what is included and how much senior time you get, not only the monthly fee.
**Should I choose a local SEO agency or a national one?** Choose based on skills. A business that serves one metro area needs strong local SEO and Google Business Profile experience. A national brand needs content and authority-building at scale, and the agency's office location matters far less.
**How long should an SEO contract be?** A short start term is reasonable, since SEO needs a few months to show direction. After that, month-to-month terms keep the agency accountable. Be cautious with long contracts that carry heavy cancellation penalties.

## How do I choose an SEO agency for AEO visibility?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/choose-seo-agency-for-aeo

**Short answer:** Choose an agency that treats AEO as an extension of solid SEO. It should fix technical access, structure content as clear answers, add accurate schema, strengthen your brand's presence across trusted sources and track citations in AI answers over time. Avoid any agency that guarantees AI citations or sells AEO as a shortcut.

- AEO helps your content get used and cited in AI and answer-style results.
- A capable agency combines technical SEO, content structure, schema and authority.
- AI visibility should be tracked with a defined prompt set over time.
- Guaranteed AI citations and "secret AI hacks" are red flags.

### What AEO means

Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the work of making your content easy for answer-style search to find, understand and quote. Answer engines include Google's AI Overviews and featured snippets, Bing Copilot, ChatGPT search, Perplexity and voice assistants. Instead of listing links, these tools give a direct answer and often cite a few sources.

AEO overlaps heavily with SEO. AI systems still depend on crawlable pages, clear content and trust signals. The difference is emphasis. AEO puts more weight on direct answers, question-led structure, entity clarity and being mentioned by sources that AI tools already rely on.

You will also hear the term generative engine optimization (GEO). People use it in slightly different ways, but it usually refers to the same goal of appearing in AI-generated answers. When you talk to agencies, ask them to define what they mean so you are comparing like for like.
### What an AEO-capable agency actually does

An agency that understands AEO will start with the basics. It checks that AI crawlers and search bots can access your pages, that your content renders properly and that important pages are indexed. Without that, nothing else matters.

From there, the work focuses on making your expertise easy to extract and trust. That includes rewriting key pages to answer questions directly, adding structured data that accurately describes your business and content, and building consistent information about your brand across your site, listings and reputable third-party sources.

- Technical access: crawlability, rendering, indexing and bot access rules reviewed.

- Answer-first content: clear questions as headings with concise answers beneath.

- Structured data: Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, FAQ or Article schema where accurate.

- Entity clarity: consistent name, services, locations and facts everywhere your brand appears.

- Authority building: earned mentions and links from sources AI tools tend to cite.

- Measurement: tracking citations and brand mentions across AI tools over time.
### Questions to ask an agency about AEO

A good agency can explain its AEO approach in plain language. Ask for specifics about process, measurement and how AEO connects to their regular SEO work. If they can't separate real tactics from buzzwords, keep looking.

Ask them to walk through a page on your own site. How would they restructure it? What schema would they add? Which questions would they target? The quality of that conversation tells you more than a proposal template.

- How do you define AEO and GEO, and how do they differ from your standard SEO work?

- Which AI tools and answer surfaces do you track, and how often?

- How do you choose the prompts and questions you monitor?

- What changes would you make to our top pages first, and why?

- How do you build the third-party mentions that AI tools draw on?

- How will you report AI visibility alongside rankings and leads?
### How AI visibility should be measured

AI answers change often. The same prompt can produce different answers on different days, in different locations and for different users. So AI visibility is best measured as a trend across a fixed set of prompts, not as a single snapshot.

A sound approach starts by defining a prompt set based on the questions your customers actually ask. The agency then checks those prompts across chosen AI tools on a regular schedule and records whether your brand is mentioned, whether your site is cited and which competitors or sources appear instead. Over time this shows whether your share of answers is moving.

AI visibility should sit alongside traditional metrics. Search Console impressions and clicks, rankings for key queries, referral traffic from AI tools where it can be identified, branded search and leads all belong in the same report. The goal is business results, and AI visibility is one input.

| Metric | What it tells you | Where it comes from |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Brand mention rate | How often your brand appears in answers to your prompt set | Manual checks or AI visibility tracking tools |

| Citation rate | How often your pages are linked as sources | Manual checks or AI visibility tracking tools |

| Competing sources | Which sites AI tools rely on instead of yours | Prompt tracking results |

| AI referral traffic | Visits arriving from AI tools where identifiable | Analytics referral data |

| Search performance | Impressions, clicks and positions for key queries | Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools |
### Red flags when hiring for AEO

AI search is new enough that some providers oversell it. The biggest red flag is a guarantee that ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google's AI will cite or recommend you. No agency controls those systems, and their outputs vary by user and over time.

Be cautious of tactics that try to trick AI systems. Hidden text, mass-produced pages stuffed with questions, fake reviews or paid placements dressed up as editorial mentions can backfire. Google's spam policies apply to content aimed at AI features as well.

Also watch for agencies that treat AEO as separate from SEO. If they propose AEO work while ignoring obvious technical problems or thin content on your site, they are skipping the foundation.

- Guaranteed AI citations or guaranteed placement in AI Overviews.

- "Secret prompts" or tricks to manipulate AI answers.

- Bulk AI-written pages with no editing, expertise or original value.

- Reports with screenshots of single answers and no consistent tracking.

- No plan for technical health or content quality.
### How Best SEO Company approaches AEO

We treat AEO and GEO as part of one SEO program. Every engagement starts with a technical review and a content audit, because AI tools can only use pages they can reach and understand. We then restructure priority pages around real customer questions, add accurate schema and tighten your brand's facts across your site and listings.

We track AI visibility with a defined prompt set, checked on a regular schedule, and report it alongside rankings, traffic and leads. We don't promise citations. We show you the trend, the sources that compete with you and the work we did to change it.

AEO work is included in our Growth plan at $3,500 per month and available as a focus within custom Scale plans. Our free 40-point audit includes a basic AI readiness review, so you can see where you stand before you commit.

**Is AEO different from SEO?** AEO builds on SEO. Both need crawlable, trustworthy, well-structured content. AEO puts extra focus on direct answers, schema, entity consistency and tracking citations in AI tools.
**Can an agency guarantee my business will appear in ChatGPT or AI Overviews?** No. AI systems decide what to show, and answers vary by user, location and time. A good agency can improve your odds and measure the trend, but it cannot guarantee a citation.
**How long does AEO take to show results?** Timelines are similar to SEO. Technical fixes and page restructuring can be picked up within weeks of recrawling, while authority and third-party mentions build over months. Track a consistent prompt set so you can see the direction of travel.

## Which SEO agencies offer top AI SEO services?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/ai-seo-services

**Short answer:** Agencies offering strong AI SEO services do two things well. They improve your visibility in AI answers through technical access, answer-first content, schema and authority, and they use AI tools responsibly to speed up research and analysis. Judge any agency by its process, measurement and transparency, and avoid anyone guaranteeing AI citations.

- "AI SEO" can mean optimizing for AI search or using AI tools to do SEO.
- The services that matter most are technical access, content, schema and authority.
- Vet AI claims by asking for process, measurement and human review.
- Choose on fit and evidence, not on who uses the most AI buzzwords.

### Why we don't rank other agencies

Many agencies now advertise AI SEO services, and lists of "top AI SEO agencies" are common. Most of those lists are written by agencies or paid for by them. We think it is more useful to show you how to judge any agency yourself, ourselves included.

The right provider depends on your business size, goals, markets and budget. A local service company and a national software brand need different things from AI SEO work. So this guide explains what the services are, which ones matter and how to test an agency's claims before you hire.
### What "AI SEO services" can mean

The phrase covers two different ideas, and agencies often blur them. The first is optimizing for AI search. That means improving how often your brand and pages appear in AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot and similar tools. This work is often called answer engine optimization (AEO) or generative engine optimization (GEO).

The second is using AI tools to do SEO. Agencies may use AI to cluster keywords, draft outlines, analyze crawl data or spot patterns in large sites. Used well, this saves time and lets specialists focus on judgment. Used badly, it produces generic content at scale with no expertise behind it.

Both can be valuable. When you talk to an agency, ask which one they mean, how they do it and how a human checks the output. A good answer covers both and explains where AI helps and where it does not.
### AI SEO service types and what to expect

The table below lists the AI SEO services you are most likely to see in proposals. Use it to understand what each service should involve and what a realistic outcome looks like. Not every business needs every service.

| Service | What it involves | What to expect |

| --- | --- | --- |

| AI readiness audit | Review of crawl access, rendering, indexing, schema and content structure for AI and answer surfaces | A prioritized fix list tied to your key pages |

| Answer-first content (AEO) | Restructuring pages around real questions with direct, accurate answers | Clearer pages that suit snippets, AI summaries and human readers |

| Structured data | Adding and validating schema that accurately describes your business and content | Eligibility for rich results and clearer entity signals |

| Entity and brand consistency (GEO) | Aligning your facts across site, listings, profiles and reputable third parties | AI tools describe your business more accurately over time |

| Digital PR and mentions | Earning coverage and links from sources AI tools tend to cite | Gradual authority gains, which are hard to fake and slow to build |

| AI visibility tracking | Checking a defined prompt set across AI tools on a schedule | Trend reporting on mentions, citations and competing sources |

| AI-assisted SEO operations | Using AI for research, clustering and analysis with human review | Faster turnaround on analysis, with specialists making the decisions |
### Which AI SEO services matter most

Start with the foundation. If AI crawlers and search bots can't reach or render your pages, no amount of content work will help. A technical review should come first, followed by the pages that drive the most business for you.

Next, focus on content that answers real questions clearly and accurately. AI tools favor pages where the answer is easy to find and the source looks trustworthy. Clear headings, concise answers, original insight and named expertise all help. Accurate schema and consistent business facts then make your content easier to interpret.

Authority is the slowest piece and often the most important. AI tools lean on sources they already trust. Earning genuine mentions in respected industry publications, local news, directories and review sites strengthens the signals both search engines and AI systems use.

- Priority 1: technical access and indexing for key pages.

- Priority 2: answer-first content on pages that drive revenue.

- Priority 3: accurate structured data and consistent entity facts.

- Priority 4: earned authority through digital PR and quality links.

- Ongoing: AI visibility tracking alongside rankings and leads.
### How to vet an agency's AI claims

Ask for the process behind every claim. If an agency says it improves AI visibility, ask how it measures that visibility, which tools it tracks, how it picks prompts and what changed for a past client. You are looking for a repeatable method and honest reporting.

Ask how the agency uses AI in its own work. Who reviews AI-assisted content? How do they check facts? How do they make sure content reflects real expertise? Google's guidance focuses on whether content is helpful and reliable, not on how it was produced, so a clear review process matters.

Finally, check the contract and the reporting. You should own your content and data, see the work completed each month and be able to leave on reasonable terms.

- Do you guarantee AI citations? (The honest answer is no.)

- Can you show a sample AI visibility report?

- How do you decide which prompts to track?

- Who reviews and edits AI-assisted content before it goes live?

- How does AI work connect to technical SEO, content and links?

That includes AI readiness audits, answer-first content, schema, entity consistency, digital PR and regular AI visibility tracking reported next to rankings, traffic and leads. **Is AI SEO the same as AEO or GEO?** Often, yes, when people mean optimizing for AI search. But "AI SEO" can also mean using AI tools to do SEO work. Ask any agency which meaning it uses so you know what you are buying.
**Will AI-written content hurt my rankings?** Google's guidance focuses on whether content is helpful and reliable, not how it was produced. Content mass-produced to manipulate rankings can violate spam policies. AI-assisted content that is edited, fact-checked and grounded in real expertise is a different matter.
**Do small businesses need AI SEO services?** Most small businesses get the most value from strong local SEO, technical health and clear service pages first. Those also help with AI visibility. Dedicated AI tracking makes more sense once the foundations are in place.
**How do I know if AI SEO work is paying off?** Look for a rising trend in brand mentions and citations across a fixed prompt set, alongside search impressions, clicks and leads. Single screenshots of one AI answer are not reliable evidence, because answers vary.

## Can you recommend an SEO tool to improve AEO?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/seo-tools-for-aeo

**Short answer:** No single tool handles AEO on its own. Start with free tools: Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools for indexing and search data, Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema.org validator for structured data, and a site audit tool for technical issues. Add Semrush or Ahrefs for research, plus an AI visibility tracker for citations.

- AEO needs a small stack of tools rather than one magic platform.
- Free Google and Bing tools cover indexing, search data and schema checks.
- Semrush and Ahrefs help with question research, competitors and links.
- AI visibility trackers measure mentions and citations over time.

### Why there is no single AEO tool

Answer engine optimization depends on several things working at once. Your pages must be crawlable and indexed, structured around real questions, marked up with accurate schema and supported by authority from other sites. Then you need a way to see whether AI tools are using your content. No single product does all of that well.

The good news is that the core stack is affordable, and much of it is free. Most businesses can cover the essentials with webmaster tools from Google and Bing, a schema validator and a site audit tool. Paid research platforms and AI visibility trackers add depth once the basics are in place.

Below we group tools by the job they do. We describe what each category helps with rather than listing features or prices, since those change often. Check each vendor's current offering before you buy.
### Free tools from the search engines

Google Search Console is the first tool every site should set up. It shows which queries bring impressions and clicks, which pages are indexed, and which have problems. It also reports on structured data it detects and on page experience. For AEO, the query data is especially useful because it reveals the questions people already associate with your site.

Bing Webmaster Tools offers similar data for Bing. That matters for AEO because Bing's index supports Microsoft Copilot and is used by other search and AI products. Submitting your sitemap and checking crawl issues in Bing is a quick, low-effort step that many businesses skip.

Both tools give you first-party data straight from the search engine. That makes them more reliable for indexing and performance questions than third-party estimates.
### Structured data testing tools

Structured data helps search engines and AI systems understand what a page is about, who published it and what entities it describes. Errors in your markup can stop it from being used. Two free tools cover most testing needs.

Google's Rich Results Test checks whether a page's structured data is eligible for Google's rich result features and flags errors and warnings. The Schema.org validator checks markup against the wider Schema.org vocabulary, including types Google does not use for rich results. Using both gives you a fuller picture.

Remember that valid schema only helps if it is accurate. Markup should describe content that is actually visible on the page. Google's structured data guidelines warn against marking up content that users can't see or that misrepresents the page.

- Rich Results Test: checks eligibility for Google rich results.

- Schema.org validator: checks markup against the full vocabulary.

- Search Console enhancement reports: track schema issues across the site over time.
### Research and competitive tools

Semrush and Ahrefs are well-known SEO platforms used for keyword research, competitor analysis, backlink analysis and site audits. For AEO, they help you find the questions people search for, see which pages rank for them and spot which sites earn links and mentions in your space.

Both platforms are paid, with different plans, and both update their feature sets regularly. Some now include features related to AI search. Check what each currently offers and use free trials where available before you commit.

If budget is tight, you can get far with Search Console query data, the "People also ask" questions in Google results and conversations with your sales and support teams. Real customer questions are the best raw material for answer-first content.
### AI visibility tracking tools

AI visibility tracking is a newer category. These tools run a set of prompts through AI assistants and search features on a schedule and record whether your brand is mentioned, whether your site is cited and which other sources appear. Several vendors offer this, and some established SEO platforms have added similar features.

Because AI answers vary by user, location and time, treat any single result with caution. The value comes from tracking the same prompt set over weeks and months and watching the trend. Pick a tool that lets you control the prompts, see the full answers and export the data.

You can also track manually. Build a spreadsheet of your most important customer questions, check them in a few AI tools each month and record mentions and citations. It takes time, but it costs nothing and helps you understand how answers are formed.
### Which tool to use for each AEO task

Use this table to match tools to the job in hand. Most businesses should start with the free tools in the first rows and add paid platforms when they need more research depth or scale.

| AEO task | Tool or category | Cost |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Check indexing and query data | Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools | Free |

| Validate structured data | Google Rich Results Test, Schema.org validator | Free |

| Quick technical and on-page check | Best SEO Company free SEO audit tool | Free |

| Question and keyword research | Semrush, Ahrefs, Search Console queries | Paid, with some free options |

| Competitor and backlink analysis | Semrush, Ahrefs | Paid |

| Track AI mentions and citations | AI visibility tracking tools or manual prompt tracking | Paid or free (manual) |
### Start with our free SEO audit tool

Our free live SEO audit tool checks a page in real time for common technical and on-page issues, including titles, meta descriptions, headings, indexability signals and structured data presence. It is a fast way to find the problems that stop search engines and AI tools from reading your pages properly.

For a deeper review, request our free 40-point audit. A specialist looks at your site's technical health, content structure, local presence and AI readiness, and sends you a prioritized list of fixes. There is no obligation to hire us.

Tools show you problems, but they don't fix them or set priorities for you. If you want help turning the data into a plan, Best SEO Company runs AEO and GEO work as part of its Growth and Scale plans, on month-to-month terms after a 90-day start.

**What is the best free tool for AEO?** Google Search Console is the most useful free starting point, because it shows real query data and indexing status from Google. Pair it with Bing Webmaster Tools, the Rich Results Test and a site audit tool for broader coverage.
**Do I need Semrush or Ahrefs for AEO?** Not to get started. They are helpful for deeper keyword, competitor and backlink research. Many small businesses can make solid progress with free tools and real customer questions first.
**Can a tool tell me exactly why AI cites a competitor instead of me?** No tool can see inside an AI system's decision. Tracking tools can show which sources are cited for your prompts, and you can compare those pages with yours for clarity, depth, structure and authority.

## How much does SEO cost?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/seo-cost

**Short answer:** Most US businesses pay for SEO as a monthly retainer. Local, single-location work often starts around $1,000 to $2,000 a month, while competitive or multi-location programs commonly run several thousand dollars or more. Price depends on competition, site size, content volume and link building. Our own plans start at $1,500 a month.

- Monthly retainers are the most common pricing model for ongoing SEO.
- Competition, locations, site size, content and links drive most of the price.
- Very cheap SEO usually means automated reports, thin content or risky links.
- Judge ROI on leads and revenue from organic search, measured over months.

### The four common SEO pricing models

SEO is sold in four main ways. Each one fits a different kind of need, and many businesses use more than one over time. The model matters because it shapes what the provider is paid to focus on.

A monthly retainer pays for ongoing work across technical fixes, content, local signals and links. It suits businesses that want steady growth, because search results keep changing and competitors keep publishing. A project fee covers a defined piece of work with a start and an end, such as a technical audit, a site migration or a content plan.

Hourly consulting buys expert time for advice, training or review while your own team does the work. Performance-based pricing ties fees to rankings, traffic or leads. It sounds safe, but it often rewards easy wins on low-value keywords and can push providers toward risky shortcuts.

| Model | Best for | Typical shape | Watch out for |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Monthly retainer | Ongoing growth and maintenance | Fixed monthly fee, scoped deliverables | Vague scope with no clear monthly output |

| Project | Audits, migrations, content plans | One-time fee per deliverable | No help implementing the findings |

| Hourly consulting | In-house teams that need direction | Billed per hour or in blocks | Advice that never turns into action |

| Performance-based | Narrow, measurable goals | Fee tied to rankings or leads | Targeting easy terms that bring no revenue |
### What drives the cost of SEO

Two businesses can ask for SEO and need very different amounts of work. The price reflects how much effort it takes to move the results you care about. A plumber in a small town and a national software company are not buying the same thing.

Competition is the biggest factor. If the pages ranking for your terms belong to large brands with years of content and links, you need more content and more authority to compete. Scope is the second factor, which covers how many pages, locations and services the work has to support.

- Competition: how strong the sites ranking for your target searches are.

- Number of locations: each location needs its own Google Business Profile work, local pages and citations.

- Site size: large sites have more technical issues, templates and pages to fix and maintain.

- Content volume: how many new pages and refreshes you need each month.

- Links and digital PR: earning real coverage and links takes research, outreach and creative work.

- Starting point: a site with penalties, migration damage or no history needs more early work.
### What you get at different budget levels

The ranges below are rough market ranges. They vary a lot by provider, region and industry, and they are not drawn from a study. Use them to sense-check quotes rather than as fixed prices.

As a concrete reference point, our Starter plan is $1,500 a month and covers local SEO for a single location. Our Growth plan is $3,500 a month for businesses that need more content, technical work and authority building. Our Scale plan is custom-priced for multi-location, enterprise or highly competitive programs. Yearly billing takes 15% off, and every plan moves to month-to-month after a 90-day start term.

At the lower end, expect focused work on a narrow set of goals. As budgets rise, you get more content each month, deeper technical work, link building and more strategic time. The jump in price should come with a clear jump in output you can see.

| Rough monthly budget | Usually fits | What the work tends to include |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Under $1,000 | Very small local businesses | Basic fixes, Google Business Profile upkeep, light reporting |

| $1,000 to $2,500 | Single-location local businesses | Local SEO, on-page work, a few content pieces, citations |

| $2,500 to $5,000 | Growing regional or online businesses | Regular content, technical SEO, link building, AI search visibility |

| $5,000 and up | Multi-location, ecommerce, competitive niches | Large content programs, digital PR, ongoing technical work at scale |
### Red flags in cheap SEO

Cheap SEO is tempting when budgets are tight. The problem is that real SEO work takes skilled time, and very low prices usually mean that time is not being spent. In some cases cheap work does damage that costs more to clean up later.

Be careful with any offer that promises page one or a number-one ranking. No one controls Google's results, so a guarantee is a sales line. Watch also for providers who will not tell you what links they build or what content they publish.

- Ranking guarantees or fixed timelines for top positions.

- Bulk link packages sold by the hundred or thousand.

- Automated reports with no human analysis or recommendations.

- Content that is thin, generic or copied across many client sites.

- Long contracts with no way out if results do not show up.

- No access to your own Search Console, Analytics or Google Business Profile data.
### How to judge SEO ROI

SEO return comes from organic visitors who turn into leads, calls, bookings or sales. Rankings and traffic are useful signals, but they are not the goal. Set up tracking for the actions that matter to your business before you judge results.

A simple way to frame ROI is to estimate the value of an organic lead or sale and compare it to what you spend. If your average job is worth a few thousand dollars, a handful of extra organic leads each month can cover a retainer. If your margins are thin, you need more volume for the same spend.

Give SEO time. Early months often go to technical fixes and content that takes a while to rank. Look for leading signs such as more pages indexed, more keywords appearing in Search Console and more local map views, then expect leads to follow as rankings improve.
### Questions to ask before you sign

A good provider can explain exactly what they will do each month and why. Ask for a sample report and a sample plan for the first 90 days. You should be able to see the work, not just a summary of it.

Ask who will do the work and how they communicate. Ask how they build links and what they do if a strategy is not working. Clear answers here tell you more than any sales deck.

- What will you deliver in the first 90 days?

- Which metrics will you report on, and how often?

- Who owns the content, links and accounts if we part ways?

- What does the contract require after the first term?

**Is SEO a one-time cost?** Some SEO work is one-time, such as an audit or a site migration. Most businesses still need ongoing work because competitors publish, search results change and new content takes time to earn rankings. That is why retainers are the most common model.
**How long before SEO pays off?** It depends on competition and your starting point. Many businesses see early signs within a few months, with more meaningful lead growth after that. Be wary of anyone who promises a fixed timeline.
**Can I do SEO myself to save money?** Yes, many small businesses handle the basics themselves, such as their Google Business Profile, simple on-page fixes and review requests. Our free 40-point audit and free SEO audit tool can show you where to start. Paid help makes more sense once competition rises or the technical work gets complex.
**Why do SEO quotes vary so much?** Providers scope work differently, and they use different mixes of senior and junior staff. One quote may include content and link building while another covers only reporting. Compare deliverables line by line, not just the monthly number.

---

## What is the best strategy for SEO?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/best-seo-strategy

**Short answer:** The best SEO strategy is the one that fits your business, competition and starting point. For most sites that means fixing technical problems first, mapping keywords to search intent, publishing content that shows real experience, linking pages internally, earning authority, strengthening local signals where relevant, and making content easy for AI answers to cite.

- No single strategy fits every business, so prioritize by your situation.
- Technical health and intent-matched pages come before link building.
- Content that shows first-hand experience is harder for competitors to copy.
- A 90-day plan with clear owners beats a long wish list.

### Why there is no one-size SEO strategy

A local dentist, an online store and a B2B software company all want more organic traffic. Their customers search in very different ways, though, and their competitors are different too. A strategy that works for one can waste months for another.

What stays the same is the order of operations. Search engines have to crawl and understand your pages before content can rank, and content has to match what people want before links can lift it. Working in that order keeps you from building on a weak base.

The framework below is the order we use. Each layer depends on the one before it. You can work on several at once, but the early layers should not be skipped.
### The prioritized SEO framework

Start with the technical foundation. Make sure important pages can be crawled and indexed, load quickly, work on mobile and are not blocked or duplicated. Fixing these issues often helps existing content perform better without writing anything new.

Next, map keywords to search intent. Group searches by what the person wants to do, such as learn, compare, buy or find a nearby business. Assign each group to one page so pages do not compete with each other.

Then build content that demonstrates experience, link it together, and earn authority. Local signals and AI search visibility come next for businesses where they apply.

- Technical foundation: crawlability, indexing, speed, mobile, clean site structure.

- Search intent and keyword mapping: one clear target and purpose per page.

- Content with experience: original detail, examples, photos and expert input.

- Internal linking: connect related pages so authority and context flow.

- Authority and links: earn mentions and links from relevant, real sites.

- Local signals: Google Business Profile, reviews, citations and location pages.

- AI search: clear answers, structured data and consistent entity information.
### Content and internal linking that compound

Content works best in clusters. A main page covers a broad topic, and supporting pages answer the narrower questions around it. Each supporting page links back to the main page, and the main page links out to each one.

Experience is what separates useful content from generic content. Include details only someone who does the work would know, such as real process steps, common mistakes, original photos and honest trade-offs. This also helps with the experience and expertise signals that search quality guidelines describe.

Internal links are one of the cheapest levers in SEO. Use descriptive anchor text, link from pages that already get traffic, and fix orphan pages that nothing links to. Review internal links every time you publish something new.
### Authority, local signals and AI search

Links still matter, but quality matters far more than count. A few links from respected sites in your industry or region do more than many links from unrelated directories. Digital PR, original data, partnerships and local sponsorships are reliable ways to earn them.

For businesses that serve a local area, the Google Business Profile is often the most important asset. Keep categories, hours and services accurate, add photos, answer reviews and post updates. Make sure your name, address and phone number match across the web.

AI answer engines pull from pages that state answers clearly and can be trusted. Lead sections with a direct answer, use plain headings that match real questions, add relevant schema markup, and keep your business details consistent everywhere they appear.
### How to prioritize by business type

Your business model decides where to put the most effort. The table below shows a sensible starting focus for common types. Treat it as a starting point and adjust once you see your own data.

If you are unsure where you stand, run a technical audit and look at which searches already bring impressions in Search Console. That shows what Google already associates with your site and where small improvements can pay off quickly.

| Business type | Start with | Then focus on |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Local service (single location) | Google Business Profile, reviews, service pages | Local links, location content, citations |

| Multi-location | Location pages and profiles for each site | Consistent data, internal linking, local PR |

| Ecommerce | Crawl and indexing control, category pages | Product content, faceted navigation, links |

| B2B or SaaS | Intent mapping, comparison and solution pages | Expert content clusters, digital PR |

| Publisher or content site | Site structure and content quality | Topical depth, refresh cycles, authority |
### A 90-day SEO plan

Ninety days is long enough to fix the foundation and get new content indexed. It is usually too short to judge the full result, so treat it as the first phase. Set clear owners for each task so work does not stall.

Review progress at the end of each month. Check indexing, impressions, rankings for target pages and leads. Move effort toward what is working and drop what is not.

| Phase | Main focus | Key outputs |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Days 1 to 30 | Audit and foundation | Technical audit, fix critical issues, set up tracking, keyword and intent map |

| Days 31 to 60 | Pages and content | Optimize priority pages, publish first content cluster, fix internal links, update Google Business Profile |

| Days 61 to 90 | Authority and refinement | Start link and PR outreach, refresh underperforming pages, add schema, review results and set next quarter's plan |
### Common SEO strategy mistakes

The most common mistake is chasing tactics before the basics are in place. Buying links or publishing dozens of posts will not help much if key pages are not indexed or load slowly. Fix the foundation first.

Another mistake is targeting keywords that do not match what you sell. High-volume terms can look attractive, but traffic that never converts costs time and money. Choose searches where the person is likely to become a customer.

Many teams also stop too early or change direction every month. SEO builds on itself, so steady work over several quarters usually beats bursts of activity. Set a plan, measure it and adjust on a regular schedule.

- Publishing many thin pages instead of fewer strong ones.

- Letting several pages compete for the same search.

- Ignoring Google Business Profile when you serve a local area.

- Judging success on rankings alone instead of leads and sales.

**Should I focus on content or links first?** Usually content first. Links help pages rank, but they work best when they point to useful pages that match search intent. Fix technical issues, build strong pages, then earn links to them.
**How often should I change my SEO strategy?** Review it every quarter. The core framework rarely changes, but your priorities should shift as you see which pages and topics perform. Big changes in your business or market are also a reason to revisit it.
**Does AI search need a separate strategy?** Mostly no. The same clear, well-structured and trustworthy content that ranks in search is what AI answers tend to cite. Add direct answers, schema and consistent business details to make your content easier to quote.

---

## What is the best SEO tool?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/best-seo-tools

**Short answer:** There is no single best SEO tool. Google Search Console is the most important free tool because it shows how Google sees your site. Pair it with Google Analytics 4 for conversions, a crawler like Screaming Frog for technical audits, and a paid suite such as Semrush, Ahrefs or Moz for keyword and backlink research.

- Start with free tools from Google and Bing before paying for anything.
- Search Console is the closest thing to a must-have SEO tool.
- Crawlers find technical issues that suites and analytics can miss.
- Paid suites help most with keyword research and competitor analysis.

### Pick tools by job, not by brand

SEO covers several different jobs, and no single tool does all of them well. Some tools show your own site's data from the search engine. Others crawl your site like a bot, and others estimate data about the wider web and your competitors.

The right setup depends on what you need to answer. A local business may only need Search Console, Analytics and its Google Business Profile. An agency or an ecommerce team will likely add a crawler and a paid research suite.

Start with the free tools. They use real data from search engines, which estimates from third-party tools cannot fully replace. Add paid tools when you have a clear question the free ones cannot answer.
### Free tools from search engines

Google Search Console shows which searches bring impressions and clicks, which pages are indexed, and what problems Google found. It also lets you inspect individual URLs and submit sitemaps. If you only use one SEO tool, use this one.

Google Analytics 4 tracks what visitors do after they arrive. Use it to see which organic landing pages lead to calls, form fills or purchases. Bing Webmaster Tools offers similar site data for Bing, which also matters because some AI assistants draw on Bing's index.

PageSpeed Insights tests a page's loading performance and Core Web Vitals, using lab data and real-user field data where available. Google Business Profile manages how a local business appears in Maps and local results, including reviews, hours and photos.

- Google Search Console: search performance, indexing and crawl issues.

- Google Analytics 4: traffic behavior and conversions from organic search.

- Bing Webmaster Tools: Bing performance, indexing and site scans.

- PageSpeed Insights: page speed and Core Web Vitals checks.

- Google Business Profile: local listing, reviews and Maps visibility.
### Crawlers and technical tools

Screaming Frog SEO Spider crawls your site the way a search engine bot would. It finds broken links, redirect chains, missing or duplicate titles, thin pages, canonical issues and much more. It is a desktop program with a free version that has a crawl limit and a paid license for larger sites.

Schema validators check your structured data. Google's Rich Results Test shows whether a page qualifies for rich results in Google, and the Schema Markup Validator at schema.org checks general schema syntax. Use both whenever you add or change markup.

A crawler is often where real technical problems show up first. Analytics shows a traffic drop, but a crawl tells you why, such as a template that started adding noindex tags or a migration that broke redirects.
### Paid all-in-one SEO suites

Semrush, Ahrefs and Moz are the best-known paid SEO suites. Each builds its own index of keywords and links, then estimates search volume, keyword difficulty, competitor rankings and backlinks. Their numbers are estimates, so use them to compare and prioritize rather than as exact counts.

Semrush is known for a broad toolkit that covers keyword research, competitor analysis, site audits, rank tracking and marketing features beyond SEO. Ahrefs is known for its backlink index and strong keyword and content research. Moz is known for its Domain Authority metric, keyword research and an approachable interface.

All three overlap heavily, and plans and features change often. Use free trials or limited free versions where offered, and pick the one whose data and workflow your team actually uses.
### Comparison by use case

Use this table to match the job to the tool. Most teams combine two or three of these rather than relying on one.

| Use case | Good starting tool | Also consider |

| --- | --- | --- |

| See how Google views your site | Google Search Console | Bing Webmaster Tools |

| Track conversions from organic search | Google Analytics 4 | Your CRM or call tracking |

| Find technical issues | Screaming Frog SEO Spider | Site audit features in Semrush, Ahrefs or Moz |

| Check page speed | PageSpeed Insights | Core Web Vitals report in Search Console |

| Keyword research | Semrush or Ahrefs | Moz, Search Console query data |

| Backlink analysis | Ahrefs or Semrush | Moz |

| Local visibility | Google Business Profile | Local rank tracking in a paid suite |

| Structured data | Rich Results Test | Schema Markup Validator |

| Quick free site check | Our free SEO audit tool | Our free 40-point audit |
### A simple tool stack for most businesses

Most small and mid-sized businesses can do a lot with a lean stack. Set up Search Console, Analytics 4 and Bing Webmaster Tools on day one. Claim and complete your Google Business Profile if you serve a local area.

For a quick health check, run your site through our free SEO audit tool at /tools/seo-audit-tool. It flags common technical and on-page issues in your browser. For a deeper review, request our free 40-point audit and a strategist will look at your site by hand.

Add a crawler and a paid suite when you start publishing content regularly or competing on harder keywords. Tools only help if someone reviews the data and acts on it, so budget time for analysis as well as subscriptions.
### Tools for AI search visibility

AI answer engines such as Google's AI features, ChatGPT and Perplexity are a newer place where people find businesses. Tooling for this area is still young, and many products only sample a set of prompts and report where a brand appears. Treat those reports as directional.

The basics still come from the tools above. Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools show whether your pages are indexed and discoverable. Schema validators confirm your structured data is correct, and a crawler checks that important content is in the HTML and not hidden behind scripts.

A practical habit is to ask AI assistants the questions your customers ask and note which sources they cite. Compare those sources with your own pages to see what is missing, such as a clear answer, a comparison or up-to-date business details.

**Can I do SEO with only free tools?** Yes, many businesses do. Search Console, Analytics 4, Bing Webmaster Tools, PageSpeed Insights and Google Business Profile cover the core data. Paid tools mainly add competitor and keyword research.
**Is Semrush or Ahrefs better?** Both are strong and overlap a lot. Ahrefs is often preferred for backlink research, while Semrush is often chosen for its broad toolkit. Try both and pick the one your team will use every week.
**Are keyword volumes in SEO tools accurate?** They are estimates built from each tool's own data, so they often differ between tools. Use them to compare keywords against each other. Search Console shows real impressions for searches your site already appears for.

---

## How can SEO be improved?
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/how-to-improve-seo

**Short answer:** To improve SEO, fix technical issues that block crawling and indexing, match each page to one search intent, refresh content that is outdated, add internal links between related pages, show real expertise and trust, earn relevant links, strengthen local signals, and measure results in Search Console and Analytics so you can repeat what works.

- Fix crawling and indexing problems before anything else.
- Refreshing existing pages is often faster than publishing new ones.
- Internal links and clear titles are high-impact, low-effort wins.
- Measure leads and conversions, not just rankings.

### Start with technical fixes

Search engines need to find, crawl and index your pages before they can rank. Technical issues can quietly hold back a whole site. Check these first because every other improvement depends on them.

Open Search Console and look at the page indexing report. Note important pages that are excluded and find out why. Then run a crawl with a tool like Screaming Frog or our free audit tool to catch broken links and redirect problems.

- Confirm important pages are indexed and not blocked by robots.txt or noindex.

- Fix broken internal links and remove redirect chains.

- Set correct canonical tags to handle duplicate pages.

- Submit an up-to-date XML sitemap in Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

- Make sure the site works well on mobile and uses HTTPS everywhere.
### Improve on-page SEO

Each page should target one main topic and the search intent behind it. Look at what already ranks for your target search. If the top results are guides, a sales page will struggle, and if they are product pages, a long article may not fit.

Write a unique title tag that includes the main phrase and gives a reason to click. Use one clear H1, logical subheadings and a meta description that summarizes the page. Add descriptive alt text to meaningful images.

Put the most useful information near the top. Answer the main question early, then add detail. This helps readers, and it makes your page easier for search features and AI answers to quote.
### Refresh content and strengthen internal links

Many sites have pages that once ranked well and slowly slipped. Search Console shows these as pages with falling clicks or impressions. Updating them is often faster than writing something new, because they already have some history and links.

When you refresh a page, update facts and examples, cover questions people now ask, remove outdated sections and improve the structure. Change the date only when the content has really changed. Merge thin pages that cover the same topic into one stronger page and redirect the old URLs.

Internal links tell search engines which pages matter and how topics connect. Link from strong, relevant pages to the ones you want to rank. Use descriptive anchor text and make sure no important page is left without internal links.
### Show experience, expertise and trust

Google's quality rater guidelines describe experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust, often shortened to E-E-A-T. These are not a single ranking factor. They describe what helpful, reliable content looks like, and the signals that support them help both people and search engines.

Show who is behind your content and why they know the subject. Use real examples, original photos and specific steps from your own work. Keep contact details, policies and business information easy to find.

- Add author bios with relevant experience and credentials.

- Include original photos, examples and process details.

- Cite reputable sources when you reference facts.

- Show reviews, licenses, certifications and a real address where relevant.

- Keep an About page and contact page that are complete and current.
### Earn links, build local signals and improve page experience

Links from relevant, trusted sites still help pages rank. Focus on earning them with useful resources, original data, partnerships, local sponsorships and press coverage. Avoid buying links in bulk, which can lead to penalties and wasted budget.

If you serve customers in a specific area, complete your Google Business Profile with accurate categories, services, hours and photos. Ask happy customers for reviews and reply to them. Keep your business name, address and phone number consistent across directories and your own site.

Page experience matters for users and supports SEO. Check key templates in PageSpeed Insights and the Core Web Vitals report. Compress images, limit heavy scripts, avoid layout shifts and remove intrusive pop-ups on mobile.
### Make content easy for AI answers to use

AI answer engines summarize pages and often cite their sources. Pages with clear structure and direct answers are easier for them to quote. The same habits also help with featured snippets in regular search.

Start key sections with a short, plain answer to the question in the heading. Use headings that match how people phrase questions. Add relevant schema markup, such as Organization, LocalBusiness, Product or FAQ where it fits, and validate it.

Keep your business name, services, locations and contact details consistent on your site, your Google Business Profile and major directories. Inconsistent details make it harder for any system to trust which version is correct.
### Prioritize by impact and effort

You cannot do everything at once. Rank tasks by how much they are likely to help and how much work they take. Start with high-impact, low-effort tasks, then plan the larger projects.

Impact varies by site. A site with indexing problems gains the most from technical fixes, while a technically clean site may gain more from content and links. Use the table as a general guide and adjust it to your audit findings.

| Task | Likely impact | Effort | When to do it |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Fix indexing and crawl blockers | High | Low to medium | First |

| Rewrite weak title tags | Medium to high | Low | First month |

| Add internal links to priority pages | Medium to high | Low | First month |

| Complete Google Business Profile | High for local | Low | First month |

| Refresh declining pages | High | Medium | Ongoing |

| Improve Core Web Vitals | Medium | Medium to high | After critical fixes |

| Publish new content clusters | High over time | High | Ongoing |

| Earn links through digital PR | High over time | High | Ongoing |
### Measure what matters

Track progress so you know which changes work. In Search Console, watch impressions, clicks and average position for priority pages. In Analytics 4, track organic conversions such as calls, form fills and purchases.

Keep a simple log of changes with dates. When rankings or traffic move, you can match the change to what you did. Review results monthly and plan the next set of tasks each quarter.

If you want a starting list, run our free SEO audit tool or request our free 40-point audit. Both give you specific issues to fix, sorted so you know where to begin.

**How long does it take to see SEO improvements?** Technical fixes and title changes can show effects within weeks once pages are recrawled. Content and link work usually takes longer to build. Results vary by competition and how often search engines crawl your site.
**What is the fastest way to improve SEO?** Fix indexing problems, improve title tags on pages that already get impressions, and add internal links to priority pages. These are low-effort tasks that can help pages you already have.
**Do I need to publish new content all the time?** Not always. Many sites gain more by improving and consolidating existing pages. Publish new content when there are real topics and searches your site does not yet cover.
**Can I improve SEO without technical skills?** You can handle a lot without code, including titles, content updates, internal links, reviews and your Google Business Profile. For crawl issues, site speed and structured data, you may need a developer or a technical SEO specialist.

---

## How to track SEO rankings
URL: https://www.bestseocompany.us/guides/track-seo-rankings

**Short answer:** Track SEO rankings by combining Google Search Console's Performance report, which shows average position from real impressions, with a rank tracker that checks fixed keywords by device and location. Add map-pack grid tracking for local businesses and manual or tool-based checks of AI answers. Report trends monthly, tied to clicks and leads.

- Search Console shows real impressions and average position, but averages hide detail.
- A rank tracker gives fixed, repeatable checks by keyword, device and location.
- Local businesses need grid tracking because map rankings change block by block.
- Report ranking trends next to clicks, leads and revenue, usually once a month.

### Start with the Search Console Performance report

Google Search Console is free and uses Google's own data, so it is the first place to check rankings. Open the Performance report, select Search results, and turn on the Average position metric alongside clicks, impressions and CTR. Switch to the Queries tab to see which searches triggered your pages, then the Pages tab to see which URLs earned those impressions. Set the date range to at least three months so short swings do not mislead you.

Average position is the mean of your topmost position each time your site appeared in results. A query where you showed at position 3 once and position 15 once averages out to 9, which matches neither real result. Position is also only recorded when an impression happens, so a page that drops off page one may show fewer impressions rather than a worse average. Read position together with impressions and clicks before you draw conclusions.

Use filters to make the data useful. Filter by country to isolate US traffic, by device to compare mobile and desktop, and by page to check a single URL's queries. The compare mode lets you set two date ranges side by side, which is the quickest way to see whether a site update or algorithm change moved your positions.

- Queries with high impressions and an average position of 8 to 20 are usually your best quick-win targets.

- A falling average position with rising impressions often means you started ranking for new, broader terms.

- Search Console data is sampled and anonymized for rare queries, so totals will not match keyword-level sums.
### Use a rank tracker for fixed, repeatable checks

A rank tracker checks a fixed list of keywords on a set schedule and records the exact position your page held at that moment. This gives you a clean history for the terms that matter most to the business, even when Search Console has little data for them. Most trackers also show which SERP features appeared, such as a map pack, People Also Ask or an AI Overview, and whether your page owned any of them.

Pick keywords that map to pages and revenue. A tracked set of 50 to 300 keywords is enough for most small and mid-sized businesses if each term ties to a specific page. Group keywords by topic or page so you can see whether a whole cluster is rising or falling, which is more meaningful than one keyword moving two spots.

Rank trackers sample results from a single location and device at a single time, so their numbers will differ from Search Console. Neither is wrong. Search Console tells you what real users saw across many contexts, and the tracker tells you what one controlled check found. You can run a quick spot check any time with our free SEO rank checker.
### Track local and map-pack rankings with a grid
